$comment: CAP: 12 prose entries across expected_shape · read_this_way · suspicious_if ·
blind_spots · decisions · review_notes · expected · known_normal · known_bad ·
do_not_reflag · how_to_investigate · limitations · constants. This file carries 8,
and descriptor.interpretation.entries must equal that number. When a 13th wants in
there are exactly two legal resolutions: PROMOTE it to a check, or DELETE it.
There is no overflow file and no overflow block.
`fences` is a RECORD block, not prose — it is not counted against the cap. It
lives here because the descriptor schema's root is additionalProperties:false

expected_shape.what: Every run LOADS. The step declares `staleness.scope:"none"` / `trigger:"none"` — no HEAD/ETag probe, no content hash, no local-cache short-circuit (the `process.argv[2]`/`[3]` path override and the `data/` GeoJSON/XLSX cache were retired per N-D5, Spec 124 R-AZ) — so an unchanged source reads inserted 0 / updated 0 and the audit table is the post-write counter block plus the declared check rows, never a skip. N-D2/N-D3 are the forced diff: the legacy read updated 158 and rewrote 1,264 tuples (158 × 8 unguarded census UPDATEs) on an UNCHANGED source; the converted merged guarded upsert makes an unchanged rerun write zero (idempotent_rerun:"zero_writes").

constants.what: `Math.round(x * 1000) / 10` (the 1-dp percentage form for tenure_owner_pct / tenure_renter_pct / couples_pct / lone_parent_pct / married_pct / university_degree_pct / immigrant_pct / visible_minority_pct / english_knowledge_pct) and `Math.round` (the INT income columns avg_household_income / median_household_income / avg_individual_income) are STORAGE-FORMAT constants living inside `buildLookup`, NOT tunables: each re-states what the column stores (11 pct cols are NUMERIC(5,2) and the 3 incomes INTEGER), so an admin knob over the rounding would silently rewrite every stored row rather than change a bound (the parcels D3 ruling; Spec 124 §5 R-BA gate E). `low_income_pct` is deliberately NOT rounded in JS — the NUMERIC(5,2) cast rounds it on the write path (Fold CF-5), so rounding it here would be a second, divergent rounding. The descriptor declares these columns `written:"step"` with no scale field, which is why the rounding literals stay inline in compute.

read_this_way.what: The publisher's vocabulary is DOMAIN DATA in compute, named here rather than made configurable: the characteristic labels (INCOME_CHARACTERISTICS, PCT_CHARACTERISTIC and every family / tenure / education / immigrant / minority / language row the pivot matches), `CONSTRUCTION_PERIODS`, `PERIOD_MAP` (the stored `period_of_construction` vocabulary), the format-2 id-row markers `'Neighbourhood Number'` / `'Neighbourhood ID'`, the suppression tokens `'...'` / `'x'` / `'F'` in `parseNumeric`, and the `Name (ID)` header regex in `parseColumnHeader`. The XLSX shape is hard-wired in the runner's `acquire.js parseXlsx`: sheet[0], header row 1, `includeEmpty`, the `''` fill and `_${n}` for null headers (the csv hard-wired-options precedent). A City relabel — renaming a characteristic row, the neighbourhood id column, or the id-row marker — makes this pivot match nothing and ZEROES a column silently, with no error and no check row: the only alarm is F2's planned `census_rows_matched` floor (N-D10). Read any surprising all-null census column as a publisher relabel first.

known_normal.what: `census_rows_matched` = 31 is NORMAL, not a defect. It is the count of census characteristic rows `buildLookup` matched (the legacy INFO audit row `matchedRows`, now `acquired.lookups["ckan:nbhd-2021-census-profile"].stats.matched_rows`), carried so the audit table keeps its row rather than going silent. It is declared `severity:"INFO"` / `blocking:false` / `limit:"viol == 0"` and never gates; N-D10 records that a WARN floor (`neighbourhoods_census_rows_matched_min` = 31) is deferred to ④ F2, deliberately not folded here.

decisions.what: The 14 census columns declare `on_empty:"preserve_null"`: a suppressed, absent or ÷0 cell keeps the STORED value rather than writing NULL. This is the legacy COALESCE / absent-row semantics reproduced exactly — legacy pushed only non-null values into its 8 UPDATEs (a nid entry was created lazily) and the bulk-5 arm was literally `COALESCE(v.col, n.col)`, so a cell the source omitted left the table value untouched (N-D2/N-D14). The census fold is PROVEN data-identical: 14 cols × 158 rows = 2,212 cells, legacy cast vs stored byte-identical 2,212/2,212 on both paths (Fold CF-5).
decisions.why: Legacy kept the stored value when a cell was omitted; writing NULL instead would ERASE a good stored census value on a partial source, a silent regression the golden would not catch because the live source has 0 omitted cells. preserve_null keeps the merge additive, matching the legacy write the goldens were captured against.

suspicious_if.what: `boundaries_loaded` < 158 (the shared `sources_neighbourhoods_floor`, FAIL) is the catastrophic-load detector. More specific: `boundary_rows_inserted` > 0 on an UNCHANGED CKAN sha256 (`b0cb5807…0233`) means a KEY RE-FORMAT — the source bytes did not move, so a new boundary row means AREA_SHORT_CODE moved or the feature count grew, not a routine change (the insert path is dead on live input, N-D1). And `census_rows_matched` dropping below 31 is a silent publisher relabel: the pivot matched fewer characteristic rows, so a census column is likely zeroing while every FAIL check still reads 0.

blind_spots.what: Two carried blind spots. (1) N-D20 — `geom` is a guard term, so a geom that drifted from its `geometry` derivation is rewritten on the next run (legacy never healed it; N-D18's census-only trigger is subsumed); 0 drift today. (2) N-D14 — a table row whose `neighbourhood_id` is ABSENT from this run's GeoJSON gets no census write at all, because the upsert only touches primary (GeoJSON-derived) rows; the legacy keyed its census UPDATEs on every matched id. Exposure is 0 (ids equal 158/158 across GeoJSON, XLSX and DB).

limitations.what: N-D16 — acquisition has NO retry (execution.network.retries 0, legacy parity): a transient CKAN 502 fails the run rather than retrying. The sole cloud failure in the ledger (run 34769829628, 2026-09-13) halted at 17/28 on an un-retried GET. N-D10 — `census_rows_matched` stays INFO and never gates: a publisher relabel that zeroes a census column passes green until ④ F2 adds the WARN floor `neighbourhoods_census_rows_matched_min`. Both are deferred to ④ (F1, F2) by design, not folded into this conversion.

fences.const: Pipeline Rehab P2 mkdir-before-download is retired with downloadFile
fences.value: acquisition is the runner's acquire.js (download + format-specific parse); acquire.js owns mkdtemp, and the pre-conversion loader's `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(destPath))` in downloadFile is gone
fences.incident: Pipeline Rehab P2 (2026-08-03): the legacy downloadFile opened its write stream into the gitignored data/ dir, which does not exist on a fresh CI checkout, BEFORE the loader's only mkdirSync ran — a fresh runner crashed on the download. The converted step never touches data/: the local cache is retired (N-D5) and acquire.js's mkdtemp owns the temp dir, so the ordering hazard cannot recur. src/tests/sources-loader-mkdir.logic.test.ts's listing of load-neighbourhoods.js is removed with the why.

fences.const: the §7.6 UNNEST batch note survives as write.js batching
fences.value: the legacy `Reference: §7.6 UNNEST batch pattern` comment (single-statement UNNEST insert) is gone; the class-A guarded upsert built by scripts/lib/step/write.js does the batching, one declared statement
fences.incident: The pre-conversion loader collected all features into parallel arrays and issued one UNNEST INSERT to make the write O(1) round-trips instead of O(features). The converted step declares `write_inventory.statements: 1`; write.js chunks the multi-row VALUES insert (158 rows fit one statement), so the batching intent is preserved by the library rather than by an inline comment that would rot against the frozen shell.

fences.const: the WF3 2026-05-08 FK-join guidance (`n.id = p.neighbourhood_id`) is UNAFFECTED
fences.value: this step never writes `id` (it is not among the descriptor's declared columns; the serial default fills it); consumers keep joining `neighbourhoods.id` to `permits.neighbourhood_id`
fences.incident: WF3 2026-05-08 established the FK-join guidance for Spec 57's consumers: lead-detail-query.ts, lead-inspect-query.ts and permits/[id]/route.ts join on `n.id = p.neighbourhood_id`. Because `neighbourhood_id` is the class-A key and `id` is a serial never projected by this step, the key-shift cohort (I-arm, `neighbourhood_id += 100000`) leaves every `id`-based FK intact — the guidance holds unchanged and is fenced here so a future re-key of the write cannot silently break it.
